taskVersion.name: ves-real-item

parts.text:
You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station Tigidam-street, Bori Metropolis. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 1148 | 3.21 | 3.21
2 | 2087 | 11.9 | 15.12
3 | 808 | 16.8 | 32
4 | 1896 | 68.5 | 100
5 | 4854 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as KHA-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station Tigidam-street, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the curve-type classification on file does not fit the layer values.

**Site Report – Station Tigidam-street, Bori Metropolis**

The VES interpretation at this station reveals a five-layer subsurface sequence. Resistivity values are: Layer 1 – 1148 Ω·m (0–3.21 m), Layer 2 – 2087 Ω·m (3.21–15.12 m), Layer 3 – 808 Ω·m (15.12–32 m), Layer 4 – 1896 Ω·m (32–100 m), and Layer 5 – 4854 Ω·m (>100 m, inferred basement or resistive substratum).

Analyzing successive triplets: Layers 1-2-3 (1148<2087>808) give **K**; Layers 2-3-4 (2087>808<1896) give **H**; Layers 3-4-5 (808<1896<4854) give **A**. This yields a KHA-type curve, consistent with the fluctuating resistivity profile — a resistive layer, underlain by a conductive layer, followed by a sequence of increasing resistivity suggestive of a resistive basement at depth.

The curve-type classification on file (KHA) correctly matches the computed layer resistivity trends and is confirmed for drilling planning purposes.

{"curve_type_stated": "KHA", "label_issue_flagged": false}
